claim.pdf_says: Table 5 — Combinations of conditions, logical operators, and parentheses; row 'simple-condition', column 'In a left-to-right sequence of elements: Element, when not first, may be immediately preceded by only:' reads "EXCLUSIVE-OR or XOR, OR, NOT, AND, ("
claim.markdown_says: | simple-condition | Yes | Yes | EXCLUSIVE-OR or XOR, OR, AND, ( | EXCLUSIVE-OR or XOR, OR, AND, ) |   (ISO_COBOL.md line 10097)
claim.why_it_matters: The transcription drops NOT from the set of elements that may immediately precede a simple-condition. As transcribed, Table 5 says a simple-condition may never follow NOT, which makes every negated simple condition ('IF NOT A = B', 'IF X AND NOT Y') illegal. It contradicts the same table's own NOT row (NOT may be immediately followed by 'simple-condition, (' ), the Table 5 NOTE ('the pair NOT (' is permissible while the pair NOT NOT is not permissible'), and 8.8.4.10 Complex negated conditions. The loss is toward falsely-restrictive syntax: legal COBOL made to look illegal. A grammar or conformance check derived from this row would reject NOT applied to a simple condition.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by direct inspection of the rendered page. Rendered specs PDF page 232 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v232/spec_p232.png; printed folio '202 (c)ISO/IEC 2023') and cropped/upscaled 2x the simple-condition row of Table 5. The printed glyphs in the 'Element, when not first, may be immediately preceded by only:' cell are unambiguous across two typeset lines: 'EXCLUSIVE-OR or' / 'XOR, OR, NOT, AND, ('. The token NOT is plainly printed between 'OR,' and 'AND,'. ISO_COBOL.md line 10097 renders that same cell as 'EXCLUSIVE-OR or XOR, OR, AND, (' -- NOT is absent. Both quotations in the claim are exact; neither source is misquoted. Adversarial checks all fail to excuse the difference: (1) The 'missing' text is NOT present elsewhere -- the entire markdown row was read in full and NOT appears nowhere in it; the omission is not reflow, wrapping, hyphenation, or a page-break artifact, since the whole table lives on this one page and the cell is a single self-contained enumeration. (2) It is not a systematic transcription convention: the markdown correctly preserves NOT in the very same column of the '(' row (line 10100: 'EXCLUSIVE-OR or XOR, OR, NOT, AND, ('), which in the PDF is typeset identically ('EXCLUSIVE-OR or' / 'XOR, OR, NOT, AND, ('). The drop is isolated to the simple-condition row. (3) The NOT row of the markdown (line 10099, 'EXCLUSIVE-OR or XOR, OR, AND, (') matches the PDF exactly, so this is not a whole-column corruption. (4) The last column of the simple-condition row matches the PDF exactly ('EXCLUSIVE-OR or XOR, OR, AND, )'), isolating the defect to one cell. The difference is meaning-changing and normative: Table 5 is part of 8.8.4.11.3 (Precedence of logical operators and the use of parentheses, ISO_COBOL.md line 10074) and the column header says 'may be immediately preceded by ONLY', i.e. the list is exhaustive and exclusive. Removing NOT from it makes 'NOT <simple-condition>' unconstructible, which is self-contradictory against the transcription's own NOT row on line 10099 ('Element, when not last, may be immediately followed by only: simple-condition, (' ) and against the transcribed NOTE on line 10103, which presupposes NOT is followed by conditions and parentheses. The bias is toward falsely-restrictive syntax, exactly the failure mode the project's spec-diagram/OCR guidance warns about.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as filed. Precise form: ISO_COBOL.md line 10097 (Table 5, section 8.8.4.11.3, PDF page 232 / printed folio 202), row 'simple-condition', column 'In a left-to-right sequence of elements: Element, when not first, may be immediately preceded by only:' should read 'EXCLUSIVE-OR or XOR, OR, NOT, AND, (' but transcribes 'EXCLUSIVE-OR or XOR, OR, AND, (' -- the token NOT is dropped. All four other cells in that row, and the NOT / '(' / ')' / connective rows, transcribe correctly (the '(' row on line 10100 retains NOT in the same column), so the fix is a single-token insertion of 'NOT, ' before 'AND, (' on line 10097. Impact: as transcribed the exhaustive ('only') predecessor set forbids NOT before a simple-condition, making every negated simple condition illegal, contradicting the same table's NOT row (line 10099) and NOTE (line 10103).
